claims.quote: Antipyretics should be administered if a fever develops.
Glucocorticoids and racemic epinephrine have not shown efficacy and are not recommended.

claims.text: Nirsevimab in the infant's first RSV season if the birth parent wasn't vaccinated.
claims.quote: Nirsevimab monoclonal antibody should be administered during the infant's first respiratory season if the birth parent has not been vaccinated.

claims.text: RSV prev: long-acting mAbs (nirsevimab, clesrovimab) give ~5 mo of protection and ↓RSV hsp;
claims.quote: Additionally, long-acting monoclonal antibodies, including nirsevimab and the recently approved clesrovimab, confer approximately 5 months of protection and significantly reduce RSV-related hospitalizations.
Monthly palivizumab prophylaxis was discontinued in 2025 due to the superior convenience of long-acting agents.
